item.name: Authentication

request.description:
For the public key, we use the ES512 algorithm. To generate this key, you can use OpenSSL as shown in the example below:

openssl ecparam -name secp521r1 -genkey -noout -out ec-p512-private.pem
openssl ec -in ec-p512-private.pem -pubout -out ec-p512-public.pem

And send the content of the ec-p512-public.pem file in the publicKey attribute.

request.description:
The clientId will be sent to the integrator during the initial setup.

The clientAssertion will be generated in the pre-request script, but we also have this example below in PHP if you want create by yourself.

$secretKey = 'YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY';
$alg = 'ES512';
$payload = [
    'iat' => Carbon::now()->timestamp,
    'exp' => Carbon::now()->addDay()->timestamp,
    'aud' => 'https://auth.kanastra.com.br/realms/{{realm_name}}/protocol/openid-connect/token',
    'iss' => 'your-client-id',
    'sub' => 'your-client-id',
    'jti' => Uuid::uuid4()->toString(),
];
$jwt_signed = JWT::encode($payload, $secretKey, $alg);

You should be authenticated after this steps, the post-request script will set the access_token on every api call, and if you have the scope permission to use you be able to test it.

item.description:
Our wallet API offers a streamlined solution for managing customized bank slip options. Below are the key services available:

Services Offered:

Create Wallet:
Set up a new wallet with custom bank slip configurations. Each wallet must be linked to a financial account. This service simplifies the creation of personalized bank slip options.

Retrieve Wallet:
Access detailed information about existing wallets. This functionality provides a comprehensive view of the wallet configurations and associated parameters.

Update Wallet:
Modify the settings of an existing wallet to accommodate new requirements. This service ensures that wallet configurations remain up-to-date with the latest bank slip parameters.

These services enable efficient management and customization of bank slips, enhancing flexibility and control over financial transactions.

item.description:
Pagamento de Boletos via API

Visão Geral

O endpoint /{account_uuid}/payments permite consultar e realizar pagamentos de boletos bancários. Existem dois fluxos possíveis:

lembre-se de se autenticar previamente.

Fluxo 1 (Consulta + Pagamento): Consulte o boleto via GET, valide os dados retornados e realize o pagamento via POST referenciando o bank_slip_payment UUID.
Fluxo 2 (Pagamento Direto): Realize o pagamento em uma única chamada POST, informando o line_code ou barcode.

Comportamento

Se pay_date = hoje → o pagamento é processado imediatamente.
Se pay_date > hoje (dia útil futuro) → o pagamento é agendado e será processado na data informada.

item.description:
1. Bank Slip Issuance:

Our bank slip service provides a simplified and efficient solution for handling financial transactions. With a straightforward approach, we present the main services available:

2. Services Offered:

Bank Slip Registration API:
Generate bank slip quickly and efficiently using a simple JSON API integration. This service offers a hassle-free method for bank slip generation, streamlining the financial transaction process.

Bank Slip Consultation:
Access detailed information about issued bank slips. This functionality provides complete visibility of the status and due dates.

PDF Bank Slip:
Your bank slip ready for payment. Obtain bank slips in PDF format for easy sharing and electronic storage. PDF issuance offers convenience in the distribution of financial documents.

Integration & Idempotency Standards

1. Overview

This document provides the technical specifications and business logic for integrating bank slip (boleto) generation via the Kanastra API. It defines how to handle identifiers, idempotency, and the specific lifecycle between Kanastra’s database and the Nuclea clearing house.

2. Field Definitions

participantControlNumber (Client or Funds Reference)

  • Definition: The primary external identifier provided by the Originator (e.g., ERP internal ID, specific fund reference, or transaction ID).

  • Priority: This is the first and preferred option for providing an external reference.

  • Validation: Maximum length of 25 characters. This limit is strictly enforced to ensure compatibility with the CNAB 400 (remittance and return files) layout.

  • Purpose: Primary field for the client’s internal reconciliation and cross-referencing with their own systems.

documentNumber (Secondary Reference)

  • Definition: A secondary external identifier (e.g., Invoice number or Contract ID).

  • Priority: This is the second option for external references.

  • Validation: Maximum length of 10 characters. This limit is strictly enforced due to the structural constraints of the CNAB 400 layout for remittance and return.

  • Note: Kanastra performs no validation (uniqueness or format) on this field; it acts as pass-through metadata within the allowed character limit.

  • Purpose: Used for additional internal mapping and reconciliation when the primary reference field is already in use.

ourNumber (Unique Identifier & Idempotency Key)

  • Definition: The primary key for the bank slip within the banking network.

  • Uniqueness: This value must be unique within your assigned wallet range.

  • Idempotency: This field must be used as the primary mechanism to prevent duplicate charges per Wallet.

item.description:
Welcome to the Commercial Note API Documentation

Before exploring the API, it is crucial to understand the concept of a Commercial Note, which plays a fundamental role in the modern business ecosystem.

A Commercial Note is a form of formal communication between companies, typically used in the context of commercial transactions. Essentially, it is a document that outlines a financial commitment between the involved parties, detailing the terms and conditions of a transaction. This document is vital for establishing and clarifying the expectations, rights, and responsibilities of both the supplier and the customer.

Commercial Notes can vary in complexity and content, depending on the nature of the transaction and the specific business practices of each sector. However, some common information generally included in a Commercial Note are:

  • Details of the involved parties: This includes the full commercial names and addresses of the companies participating in the transaction.

  • Quantities and prices: The number of units of products or hours of services, along with the unit and total prices.

  • Payment terms: The agreed payment conditions, including deadlines and accepted payment methods.

  • Legal and compliance information: Any relevant legal provisions, such as consumer protection laws or tax regulations, applicable to the transaction.

Moving forward, you will find the endpoints for registering information and issuing the commercial note.

item.description:
3. Types of PIX Keys (DICT)

The API supports four main types of keys: Random, Email, Phone, and Document (CPF/CNPJ).

Below are the types of identifiers supported by DICT.

Key Type Description Example
Phone Number Must be a valid mobile number in international format. +5511998765432
Email Any valid email address. user.example@email.com
CPF Individual Taxpayer Registry, used for personal accounts. 12345678901
CNPJ National Registry of Legal Entities, used for business accounts. 12345678901234
EVP (Random) Virtual Payment Address: a random alphanumeric value. 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426655440000

3.1. Rules for Key Creation

  • Random Key (EVP): Creation occurs asynchronously. The key is generated by BACEN, and to obtain it, the account’s key listing endpoint must be queried after the request.

  • Document Key (CPF/CNPJ): The API will automatically use the account holder’s document to register the key.

  • Email or Phone Key: The user must prove ownership of the email or phone number. This process is carried out through the validation of an OTP (One-Time Password) sent to the respective contact.

Note: There is a limit on the number of active keys per account.

  • Individual Account (PF): Up to 10 active keys.

  • Business Account (PJ): Up to 25 active keys.

3.2. Status Possibilities for Keys

Each PIX key can have one of the following statuses:

  • CREATED – The key has been successfully created in the system but is not yet active.

  • ACTIVE – The key is fully active and can be used for transactions.

  • CANCELED – The key has been deactivated or removed and cannot be used.

  • FAILED – The creation or activation of the key failed due to an error.

  • WAITING_OTP_TOKEN – The key requires the user to validate ownership via an OTP (One-Time Password) before it becomes active.

These statuses help track the lifecycle of each key and determine its current usability.

request.description:
This endpoint retrieves deposit information for a specific financial account identified by account_uuid. It allows users to check the status and details of deposit transactions associated with the given account.

Path Variables

account_uuid: A unique identifier for the account whose deposit information is being requested.

Response Structure

Upon a successful request, the API will return a JSON object containing the following fields:

  • count (integer): Total number of deposits returned.

  • next (string): URL to retrieve the next page of results, if applicable.

  • previous (string): URL to retrieve the previous page of results, if applicable.

  • results (array): A list of deposit transaction objects, where each object contains:

    • uuid (string): Unique identifier of the deposit.

    • senderBank (object): Information about the sender's bank, including:

      • code (string): Bank code.

      • name (string): Bank name.

      • comp (string): Bank compensation code.

      • ispb (string): ISPB code of the bank.

      • isParticipantComp (boolean): Indicates if the bank is part of the compensation system.

      • isParticipantPix (boolean): Indicates if the bank participates in PIX.

      • isParticipantStr (boolean): Indicates if the bank participates in the STR system.

    • createdAt (string): Timestamp when the deposit was created.

    • updatedAt (string): Timestamp when the deposit was last updated.

    • externalId (string): External identifier associated with the deposit.

    • endToEndId (string): Unique end-to-end transaction identifier.

    • amount (string): Deposit amount.

    • reconciliationId (string|null): Identifier for reconciliation, if available.

    • status (string): Current status of the deposit.

    • initType (string): Indicates how the transaction was initiated.

    • senderAccount (string): Sender’s account number.

    • senderAccountType (string): Type of the sender’s account.

    • senderBranch (string): Sender’s bank branch.

    • senderName (string): Name of the sender.

    • senderGovernmentId (string): Government-issued ID of the sender.

    • description (string|null): Description of the deposit, if available.

    • transactionId (string): Unique transaction ID.

    • product (string): Product type associated with the deposit.

    • resourceUuid (string): Resource UUID linked to the transaction.

    • feeAmount (string): Amount charged as transaction fees, if any.

    • isInternalTransfer (boolean): Indicates whether the deposit is an internal transfer.

    • receiverPixKey (string): The PIX key of the receiver.

item.description:
Performs a real-time funds transfer using the Brazilian Central Bank’s PIX instant payment system. Once the deposit is authorized, the amount is immediately credited to the recipient’s account, 24/7, including weekends and holidays.

How it works

  1. Initiation → The payer selects the recipient’s PIX key or scans a QR code.

  2. Authorization → The payer’s bank authenticates the transaction.

  3. Settlement → Funds are transferred instantly via the SPI infrastructure.

  4. Confirmation → The recipient receives immediate confirmation of the deposit.

Key Features

  • Instant settlement → Funds are available within seconds.

  • 24/7 processing → Works on weekends and holidays.

  • PIX key support → CPF/CNPJ, phone, email, or random key.

  • QR code integration → Accepts both static and dynamic QR codes.

  • Secure → Fully regulated and encrypted by the Central Bank of Brazil.

item.description:
5. Introduction to Pix QRCodes

Here we provide technical information regarding the initiation of Pix payments via QR Codes in Brazil. It follows the specifications defined by the Central Bank of Brazil (BACEN) and complies with the BR Code standard, which adopts the EMV QR Code Payment System (EMV-QRCPS) format.

5.1. Initiation via QR Code

5.1.1. General Information on Pix QR Code Initiation

The BR Code is the standard used for generating QR Codes in Brazil. It follows the EMV standard for QR Code payment systems (EMV-QRCPS).

Note: The BR Code standard applies only to the Merchant Presented Mode (MPM).

The Pix QR Code acts as a mechanism for providing or pre-filling payment information for initiating Pix transactions. It strictly adheres to the BR Code specifications, as defined in the official BR Code Manual.

5.1.2. Authorized Entities to Issue a Pix QR Code

The following entities are authorized to generate a Pix QR Code:

  1. Payment Service Providers (PSPs) of the payee.

  2. The National Treasury Secretariat (STN).

5.1.3. Contents of a Pix QR Code

A Pix QR Code can contain up to two types of information:

  • Payment Data — Standard Pix payment details such as amount, description, and recipient.

  • Recurring Payment Parameters — Configuration data for recurring transactions.

Once the QR Code is generated, the payer can scan it and follow the respective flows based on the data retrieved.

When installed on the payer’s mobile device, the PSP application is used to scan the QR Code. Upon scanning:

  • The app accesses the backend service provided by the payee’s PSP.

  • This backend is responsible for:

    • Generating the payment order.

    • Handling recurrence requests.

    • Or managing both, depending on the configuration.

5.2. Types of QR Codes

Below is a summarized overview of the different types of Pix QR Codes. The following sections describe each type in detail, including examples.

5.2.1. Static QR Code

The Static QR Code provides a limited set of functionalities. In this type of QR Code, all data required for payment initiation (configurations) are fully contained within the QR Code itself.

There are five configuration options, where:

  • One is mandatory:
    The user generating the static QR Code must provide a valid Pix key registered in the DICT (Directory of Transactional Account Identifiers), as defined by the DICT Operational Manual.

  • Four are optional:

    1. Transaction ID — Used for payment reconciliation.

    2. Free-text field — Custom text that can be displayed to the payer.

    3. Payment amount — Predefined value for the transaction.

    4. Cash-out facilitator identifier — Identifies a third-party cash withdrawal facilitator.

5.2.2. Dynamic QR Code

The Dynamic QR Code offers a broader set of functionalities, such as:

  • Payment reconciliation using a transaction ID.

  • Predefined payment amounts.

  • Structured free-text fields for presenting additional information.

Like the static QR Code, the dynamic QR Code must also include a valid Pix key from the DICT.

The key characteristic of a dynamic QR Code is its flexibility. Its internal structure is configured with a URL.

The dynamic QR Code itself contains only basic information about the payee. All other payment details are retrieved via the endpoint of the payee’s PSP, as indicated by the URL.

5.2.3. Composite QR Code

The Composite QR Code combines the functionalities of both static and dynamic QR Codes while adding support for recurring payments.

Key characteristics:

  • Includes all functionalities from the Static QR Code and the Dynamic QR Code (except for Pix Saque and Pix Troco).

  • Contains a structured definition of parameters for recurring payments.

  • Introduces a second URL field dedicated to recurrence configuration.

The main distinction of the composite QR Code is this additional URL, located in a dedicated field within the BR Code. Its payload contains recurring payment configuration details offered by the payee to the payer.

5.2.4. Pix QR Code Types Comparison

QR Code Type Dynamic or Static Fixed Amount? Payer Can Change Amount Settlement Reusable Due Date Support Fines / Interest / Discounts Main Use Case
Static QR Code Static ✅ / ❌ Depends Standard ✅ Yes ❌ No ❌ No Processing payments through an abstract representation of a PIX key.
Dynamic QR Code Dynamic ✅ / ❌ Depends Standard ❌ No ❌ No ❌ No One-time payments, traceable transactions
Dynamic QR Code Due Dynamic ✅ Yes ❌ Usually Standard or Scheduled ❌ No ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Invoices, Pix boletos, installment payments

5.3. Parameters Possibilities

The amountType (string) parameter has two possible values:

  • FIXED – The amount is fixed and cannot be changed by the payer.

  • CUSTOM – The amount can be entered or modified by the payer at the time of payment, allowing flexibility.

The type (string) parameter most important values are:

  • STATIC_QR_CODE and DYNAMIC_QR_CODE.

PIX Payments API - Documentation

1. Introduction

The Pix Payments API facilitates the initiation and confirmation of payments using all methods available within Pix, the Brazilian instant payment system regulated by the Central Bank of Brazil (BACEN).

Pix can be used by individuals (PF) and businesses (PJ) to make transfers, pay bills, and collect taxes and service fees.

2. Security and Compliance

Pix transactions are backed by strict security and compliance measures established by BACEN. All participants must follow the rules related to the use of the Pix brand and the user experience standards.

These requirements ensure the security and integrity of all operations within the Instant Payment System (SPI).

item.description:
This documentation outlines the webhook events related to CNAB file processing for bank slips. The events are designed to provide notifications about different processing stages and issues:

  • BANK_SLIP_CNAB_INVALID: Triggered when the CNAB file is invalid.

  • BANK_SLIP_CNAB_VALIDATION_ERROR: Triggered when there are validation errors.

  • BANK_SLIP_PROCESSING_ERROR: Triggered when there are processing errors.

  • BANK_SLIP_CNAB_PROCESSED: Triggered when the CNAB file has been successfully processed.

Webhook Payload Structure

Each event dispatches a JSON payload with details about the processing of the CNAB file. Below is the structure of the payload for these events:

{
  "data": {
    "errors": [],
    "totalLineProcessed": 0,
    "totalLineErrors": 0,
    "fileName": "",
    "cnabFileStatus": ""
  },
  "event": "",
  "product": "BANK_SLIP"
}

Payload Details

  • data:

    • errors: An array containing detailed error messages or codes that occurred during the processing of the CNAB file.

    • totalLineProcessed: Total number of lines that were successfully processed.

    • totalLineErrors: Number of lines that encountered errors during processing.

    • fileName: Name of the CNAB file that was processed.

    • cnabFileStatus: Current status of the CNAB file (e.g., PROCESSED).

  • event: Specifies the type of event triggered (BANK_SLIP_CNAB_INVALID, BANK_SLIP_CNAB_VALIDATION_ERROR, BANK_SLIP_PROCESSING_ERROR, BANK_SLIP_CNAB_PROCESSED).

  • product: BANK_SLIP

This documentation provides a comprehensive guide to the webhook events related to bank slip processing. The events notify subscribing systems of changes or updates to bank slips, facilitating real-time updates and responses:

  • BANK_SLIP_SETTLED: Triggered when a bank slip has been fully settled.

  • BANK_SLIP_CANCELED: Triggered when a bank slip has been canceled.

  • BANK_SLIP_OPEN: Triggered when a bank slip is created and open for payment.

  • BANK_SLIP_REJECTED: Triggered when a bank slip has been rejected.

  • BANK_SLIP_EXPIRED: Triggered when a bank slip has expired without payment.
